videos.script: Lesson 3 built a VPN on TLS. This one puts two VPNs into service, the way an administrator does it. {{keys}} WireGuard first. Each machine makes a pair of keys, and the private one never leaves the file it was written to. {{config}} The configuration is about a dozen lines. An address, a port, a key, and one block for each peer. {{up}} You will bring the tunnel up on a kernel that cannot run it, and see what stands in. Then you will read the first four packets it sends. Two of them are the whole handshake. {{handshake}} Next comes the idea that makes WireGuard different. One list of addresses per peer decides where a packet goes out, and which packets may come in. Remove one line from it, and an office goes quiet without a single error. {{allowed}} A laptop at home, behind a router doing NAT, is found without anybody typing its address. And with the wrong key, nothing answers at all. {{silence}} Last comes OpenVPN, with a key that hides even its handshake from the ISP, and a file that names each person connected. {{openvpn}} By the end you can choose between the two, and say why. {{table}}
